title: AP reports mixed Asian markets and higher U.S. futures ahead of Anthropic debut
summary: The Associated Press reported that Asian stock markets were mixed and U.S. stock futures rose as investors awaited Anthropic’s market debut. Reuters reported that Anthropic said its IPO was priced at $83 per share, above its previously targeted range. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP reported market movements and cited individual index levels and company share prices.
Reuters reports market movements and quotes Capital.com analyst Kyle Rodda; it attributes the IPO price to Anthropic.

responses.text: According to Reuters, Anthropic said its IPO was priced at $83 per share, above its previously targeted range.

title: AP and Reuters sources report damage to Riyadh tower housing Saudi wealth fund
summary: A Riyadh tower housing Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund sustained damage, according to a witness cited by AP and three people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. The Saudi-led coalition said falling debris from a missile threat it attributed to the Houthis caused material damage, with the extent still being assessed. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: A witness who requested anonymity because of security concerns described visible damage to the tower.
Three people familiar with the matter reported damage to the tower; a Reuters witness described closures and evacuations in the financial district.

responses.text: The coalition said it had dealt with a Houthi missile threat toward Riyadh and that its initial assessment indicated material damage from falling debris, with the extent still being assessed.
Reuters reported that PIF said it would respond to the agency’s request for comment.

title: TechCrunch reports Anthropic shares began Nasdaq trading above their $83 offering price
summary: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic shares traded at $110 in their first minutes on Nasdaq, above the $83 offering price. Anthropic announced that it priced its IPO at $83 per share and expected trading to begin November 19 under the symbol ANT. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Reports the shares' trading price in the first minutes of availability.
Reports the opening trade directly, without attributing it to TechCrunch.
Reports the opening trade directly; its report also includes comments from market participants.
Reports the opening trade directly in its live coverage; separately attributes an earlier pre-open indication to Bloomberg.

responses.text: The company announced that it priced its IPO at $83 per share and expected its shares to begin trading on Nasdaq on November 19 under the symbol ANT.

title: AP: Ueland pledges independence at Senate hearing on GAO nomination
summary: The Associated Press reported that comptroller general nominee Eric Ueland told senators he would act independently as Democrats questioned his independence. Government Executive reported that Ueland pledged to fulfill the office’s responsibilities and call matters as he saw them. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Reported from the confirmation hearing and quoted Ueland and senators.
Reports testimony from the hearing, Ueland’s remarks to reporters afterward, and a committee aide’s account.
Reports exchanges between Ueland and senators at the hearing and cites GAO reports.
Reports hearing testimony and remarks made to its reporter afterward by Ueland and senators, as well as an unnamed GAO employee’s account.

responses.who: Eric Ueland, nominee for comptroller general
responses.text: According to AP, Ueland told lawmakers he would act in a nonpartisan manner and fulfill the comptroller general’s responsibilities.

title: AP and CNN report flooding and water rescues in Florida’s Brevard County
summary: Flooding prompted evacuations and water rescues in Florida’s Brevard County on Thursday, according to AP and CNN. County spokesperson Don Walker told CNN that more than 50 water rescues had been conducted and rescues were continuing Thursday morning. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP cites residents, the National Weather Service, local authorities and the Florida Division of Emergency Management.
Brevard County spokesperson Don Walker told CNN that more than 50 water rescues had been conducted; the report also cites the Weather Prediction Center.
WFTV reports flash flood warnings and Doppler radar rainfall estimates for Brevard County.

responses.text: AP reported that the city ordered mandatory evacuations for some Palm Bay Estates residents, helped residents by boat and opened shelters.
Walker told CNN that more than 50 water rescues had been conducted and that rescues were continuing Thursday morning.

title: Intuit says it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion
summary: Intuit said it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for approximately $3.68 billion, with closing expected in early 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. Bending Spoons confirmed the agreement and said Intuit would invest $368 million of the proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Intuit's announcement
Attributes the acquisition announcement to Bending Spoons; cites FactSet for analyst estimates.

responses.text: Intuit said the sale would sharpen its focus on business customers and that it intended to use cash proceeds for share repurchases after closing.
Bending Spoons confirmed an agreement to acquire Mailchimp at an enterprise value of $3.68 billion and said Intuit would invest $368 million of the proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons equity.

title: White House official confirms to CBS News that national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving
summary: White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, a White House official told CBS News. Axios also reported his departure, citing its sources. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Sources; Reuters and the Daily Beast attribute details of the departure to Axios.
A White House official.

responses.text: Confirmed to CBS News that Cairncross will leave his position.

title: Senate passes permitting bill 62–33, CBS News reports; House approval still required
summary: CBS News reported that the Senate voted 62–33 to pass a bipartisan bill intended to speed permitting for energy and infrastructure projects; Axios independently reported the vote and said House approval remained necessary. CBS reported that a spokesperson said earlier in November that House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries supported permitting reform but considered the Senate legislation deficient in several areas. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Reports the Senate vote and quotes senators and a spokesperson.
Independently reports the Senate vote and describes the bill's provisions.
Reports the Senate vote and identifies senators who supported or opposed the measure.

responses.who: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, through a spokesperson
responses.text: CBS News reported that the spokesperson said earlier in November that Jeffries supported permitting reform but considered the Senate legislation deficient in several areas.

title: Russia says it struck Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv officials report bridge damage
summary: Reuters reported that Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces struck Ukrainian energy and transport infrastructure, defence industry facilities and vessels. AP reported that Kyiv authorities described damage to bridges and transport infrastructure. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Russia’s Defence Ministry statement
AP attributes its report on the Kyiv strikes to local authorities, the Kyiv City Military Administration, Mayor Vitali Klitschko and energy provider DTEK.

responses.text: The ministry said its forces struck Ukrainian infrastructure and vessels it said were used for military purposes.
Klitschko said strikes damaged the Podilskyi and Darnitskyi bridges and hit the Southern Bridge, causing traffic closures and restrictions.

title: AP reports Iraqi security forces established headquarters near Jurf al-Sakhar
summary: Iraqi security forces established a command headquarters on the outskirts of Jurf al-Sakhar, the Associated Press reported. Armed forces spokesman Sabah al-Numan said forces had begun redeploying and the prime minister had authorized the headquarters to maintain security and enforce the law, according to The National. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP reported from Baghdad and published photographs of the security deployment.
Cites remarks by government spokesman Sabah al-Numan at a media conference and an Iraq expert who spoke to The National.
Reports remarks by security officials at a joint news conference, photos obtained by 964media, and a senior government official who spoke to the outlet.

responses.who: Sabah al-Numan, spokesman for Iraq's commander-in-chief of the armed forces
responses.text: According to The National, al-Numan said forces had begun redeploying and the prime minister had given the headquarters full authority to maintain security and enforce the law in the area.
